jobs.title: CEO – PE Backed Hydraulic Cylinder and Valve Manufacturing Company
jobs.description:
Salt Creek Capital is seeking a Chief Executive Officer and investment partner to lead a portfolio company, a leading manufacturer of hydraulic cylinders, valves and related components, through a recapitalization and the next phase of its growth. The successful candidate will partner with Salt Creek Capital as an incoming investor and transaction partner, assuming the full-time, day-to-day management of the Company with full P&L responsibility.

Headquartered in Santa Ana, California, the Company is a well-known supplier of high-quality hydraulic cylinders, valves, and related components used across more than ten industry segments, including heavy machinery and industrial manufacturing equipment. With over 80 years of operating history, the Company operates out of a 26,000 square foot leased facility with 30 employees. Roughly 80% of its product line is engineered to customer specification, and the Company is the sole source for certain of its proprietary valve and steering cylinder products. That position has translated into durable customer relationships across OEMs, distributors and end users, with the majority of its top customers retained for 10-20+ years and low customer concentration.

This role will serve as the most senior business executive at the Company, will have full P&L responsibility, and shall report to and participate on the Company’s board of directors.

Key areas of responsibility include:

Work with Salt Creek Capital and the Board of Directors to develop a 3–5-year strategic plan that follows best practices of value creation
Actively engage in sales, operations, finance, supplier relations, team recruiting & development, and other functional aspects of the company's management team
Lead efforts to expand the Company’s existing network of customers through effective business development and marketing strategies
Foster continuing relationships with key customers and ensure high levels of customer service to maintain retention of current customers
Deliver strong financial performance and timely reports to the Board of Directors; oversee all company financial management and operating metrics
Evaluate and select software and system upgrades to improve operating efficiencies and data-based decision making
Expand plant automation and material handling capabilities to improve operating efficiency and production capacity

Qualifications:

Proven track record of driving change, optimizing performance, and aligning cross-functional teams around a clear vision for growth and operational excellence
Prior successful P&L management and/or CEO experience in industrial material manufacturing is highly desired
Demonstrated ability to increase profitability through proactive business development efforts
Desire to participate as a business partner and ability to balance fiduciary responsibilities to multiple stakeholders
Entrepreneurial thinker with an appetite to take on a high level of responsibility
Demonstrated experience in customer-focused business model
Successful experience implementing and operating lean manufacturing principals
Proven ability to manage all aspects of a company
At least 10 years of senior management experience
Excellent professional references and high integrity

Compensation:

The compensation package includes a competitive base salary and comprehensive health benefits. The role offers significant financial upside through equity incentive tied to value creation and company performance. Future long-term incentive opportunities may be considered based on company milestones and individual contributions. Additional details will be discussed during the interview process.

Selection Process:

Interested candidates are invited to submit resumes and cover letters to Salt Creek Capital. Candidates with appropriate backgrounds shall be asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement.Selected candidates will then be invited to proceed to phone and in-person discussions.

About Covenant House Greater Washington

For 30 years, Covenant House Greater Washington (CHGW) has been the region's leading nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering youth ages 18–24 who are experiencing homelessness, disconnection, and exploitation. Our mission is to empower, safeguard, and serve youth experiencing homelessness, disconnection, and exploitation in the Greater Washington region.

We create tailored solutions for each young person that goes beyond short-term housing and support.

Our approach equips youth with the resources they need to overcome common obstacles and barriers. Aside from housing, youth receive workforce readiness, job/career placement, post-secondary support, case management, mental health support, drop-in services, and more.

Our mission is to empower, safeguard and serve youth experiencing homelessness, disconnection, and exploitation in the Greater Washington region. The wrap-around supportive services provided to opportunity youth include housing, workforce readiness, job placement, and drop-in services.

Immediacy: Homeless youth come to Covenant House in crisis. Immediately and without question, we meet their basic human needs – a nourishing meal, a shower, clean clothes, medical attention, and a safe place away from the dangers of the street.

Stability: Homeless youth never know how they will get their next meal or where they will sleep. Covenant House provides the stability and structure necessary to build a positive future.
Choice: Young people often feel powerless to control their lives and fall into a self-defeating cycle of failure. Covenant House fosters confidence, encouraging young people to believe in themselves and make smart choices about their future.

Job Duties:

The Gift Officer I – Director of Advancement – identifies and cultivates relationships with donor prospects at major, principal and/or estate giving levels, develops and implements fundraising plans, and works collaboratively with other Advancement staff to meet predefined gift contribution goals.

This position is a member of the frontline development team whose primary responsibility is revenue generation through relationship-based fundraising activities. This individual manages a portfolio of 75 - 125 high-capacity, high-affinity prospects and develops a strategy for each prospect moving them closer to gift solicitation. This individual is strategic and thoughtful, using their strong communication and interpersonal skills to meet metrics as set forth by the Assistant Vice Chancellor for Development, being as productive as possible while employing efficient strategies for success.

the ability to conceive and ask thoughtful questions and to adjust communication and engagement strategies to meet philanthropic goals;
excellent listening skills and a professional who prioritizes long-term partnerships over transactional fundraising;
strategic thinking skills and being informed on fundraising trends and donor behavior; and
problem solving abilities that assist in overcoming challenges.
